4. URINE

Colour | Significance
Straw | Normal urine
Colourless-pale | Dilute urine: low S.G.
Deep yellow | Concentrated: dehydration, bilirubinuria
Orange-red | Haematuria, haemoglobinuria
Brown-black | Myoglobinuria
Milky white | Pyuria
Orange | Certain drugs: oxytetracyclines

facts: A clear to slightly cloudy lochial discharge can be evaluated 7 days post calving.
Metritis presents with abnormal, foul, often reddish discharge seen behind the cow in stalls.
Straw-coloured urine signifies normal bovine urine.
Colourless to pale urine indicates dilute urine with low specific gravity (S.G.).
Deep yellow urine indicates concentrated urine caused by dehydration or bilirubinuria.
Orange-red urine signifies haematuria or haemoglobinuria.
Milky white urine signifies pyuria (pus/white blood cells in urine).
Orange urine is associated with administration of certain drugs such as oxytetracyclines.
Under section '5. UDDER AND MILK', abnormal milk can be inspected using sample test vials and paddle-based testing (such as CMT) showing mastitis gel reactions.

Is the following statement true or false? 'Brown-black urine in cattle indicates pyuria.'

options.A: True, because brown-black indicates purulent matter in urine.
options.B: False, because brown-black urine indicates myoglobinuria, whereas pyuria causes milky white urine.
options.C: False, because brown-black urine indicates normal hydration.
options.D: True, because myoglobinuria causes straw-coloured urine.
